name: Question 2
problem: What is ${\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{j}=a+jΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=-5{x}^{-2},$ the lower bound is $a=-4,$ and the upper bound is $b=-2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{-2-(-4)}{n}=\frac{2}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{-2}-5{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+j\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(-4+\frac{2j}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[-5{(-4+\frac{2j}{n})}^{-2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

What is ∫−4−2−5x−2dx expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?

a
limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(−2+4jn)−2⋅4n]
b
limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(4+2jn)−2⋅2n]
c
limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(jn)−2⋅1n]
d
limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(−4+2jn)−2⋅2n]
e
limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(4jn)−4⋅4n]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1f(xj)⋅Δx,

where Δx=b−an and xj=a+jΔx.

In the definite integral

∫−4−2−5x−2dx,

the function is f(x)=−5x−2, the lower bound is a=−4, and the upper bound is b=−2. So, we have

Δx=−2−(−4)n=2n,

and therefore

∫−4−2−5x−2dx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1f(xj)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[f(−4+j⋅2n)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[f(−4+2jn)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑j=0n−1[−5(−4+2jn)−2⋅2n].
